name: Nile Valley / Kush dynastic trunk: Kerma → Kush → Napata → Meroe
description: The succession of Nubian state-forms from the earliest recorded Kerma culture through the Kushite kingdom, its Napatan phase (including the 25th Dynasty conquest of Egypt), and its final Meroitic phase. These represent one of the world's oldest continuous state traditions outside of Mesopotamia and Egypt, and the longest-lived Black African kingdom in antiquity.
ethical_notes: Kush, Napata, and Meroe are often collapsed into a single undifferentiated 'Kushite' entity by Egyptocentric historiography that treats them as footnotes to Egyptian history. Each represents a distinct phase of Nubian state-formation with its own capital, culture, and political logic. The Napatan/25th Dynasty conquest of Egypt (c. 744-656 BCE) — in which Nubian pharaohs ruled all of Egypt — is systematically minimized in Western curricula despite representing a complete reversal of the typical civilizational power gradient. Meroitic script remains only partially deciphered; our confidence in internal political succession is accordingly limited. NOTE (ADR-005/ETHICS-001, 2026-07-02): the Meroitic-phase node was removed from this chain because the 'Meroe' entity was deprecated as a duplicate of Kush (v6.85 merge map 52←552), which is already this chain's seq-1 node and whose span (-1070..350) includes the Meroitic phase (c. -300..350, capital at Medewi/Meroë, Meroitic script, iron industry, ruling Kandakes). The phase remains part of the historical record via the Kush entity and the Napata node; a dedicated native-named Meroitic-phase entity (like the Napata one) is open future work, not an erasure.

sources.citation: Shinnie, P.L. 'Meroe: A Civilization of the Sudan' (1967)

links.description: Kerma was destroyed by the Egyptian New Kingdom (18th Dynasty) under Thutmose I c. 1500 BCE. The region was incorporated into Egypt as 'Kush' for roughly 500 years before an indigenous Kushite state re-emerged at Napata.

The Kushite kingdom under Alara and Kashta consolidated around Napata and began northward expansion into Egypt. The 'Napata' entity represents this specific capital-centered political phase of 25th Dynasty rule.
links.ethical_notes: The 25th Dynasty Kushite pharaohs (Piye, Shabaka, Taharqa) ruled all of Egypt c. 744-656 BCE. Taharqa is mentioned in the Bible (2 Kings 19:9) as a military opponent of Assyria. This African empire governing the canonical 'cradle of civilization' is an inconvenient reversal of assumed civilizational hierarchies and is frequently marginalized in Western historiography.

links.description: After Assyrian invasions drove Kushite rulers from Egypt (664 BCE) and the Egyptian pharaoh Psamtik II sacked Napata itself (593 BCE), the political and economic center shifted south to Meroe. This transition marks the beginning of the distinctly Meroitic phase of Kushite civilization.

The Kushite kingdom's primary royal, political and burial focus shifted south toward Meroe (Begrawiya) by c. 300 BCE (Meroe was already significant earlier, and Napata retained religious weight); the Meroitic period developed its own script, large-scale iron industry and the ruling Kandake (Candace) queens, and the kingdom endured until its conquest by Aksum c. 350 CE.
links.ethical_notes: Restored as a distinct Meroitic phase-entity (ETHICS-015/023) after being wrongly deprecated as a duplicate of Kush in v6.85; the earlier merge conflated the Meroitic phase with the umbrella Kingdom of Kush (#52, Q241790).
